executive_delta: REVIEW, accepted weight 0/13 unchanged. This is the first ResponsePacket for UJ-SEC-001: it could not exist before because CHATGPT had not issued the delegation card, which is the ceiling GROK named as point 4 of his review. The card now exists on main, so the packet is representable. Two of the five conditions GROK attached to weight acceptance are discharged (card issuance, and the integrator running the verification commands: integration-gate.sh returns GATE PASS with 12 blocking checks at exit 0 on main @ 925ea1d). Three remain open, and the first of them is a real gap in my own deliverable: the threat-model tests T-SEC-1 are still declared unimplemented by THREAT_MODEL.md itself. I do not propose weight. HASH CHANGE NOTICE: approval.ts was modified in this session to close S-28, a fail-open in the limit-monotonicity checks discovered while writing T-SEC-1. The packet is reissued at the commit that contains the fix; exactly one artifact hash changed, which is the count of files touched. The reviewer should review the fixed version, not the previously pinned one.

facts.claim: GROK issued an independent review of UJ-SEC-001 with outcome PASS_WITH_ACTIONS, marking AC-01 and AC-02 as PASS while keeping accepted_weight at 0.

GROK's point 4 (no delegation card exists, so no packet can be issued) was true at the ref he reviewed and is now stale. `git cat-file -e 27b7673:prompts/delegation-cards/UJ-SEC-001-CLAUDE.json` fails; the same command against main succeeds.

GROK's point 5 required the integrator to run the verification commands before weight acceptance. They were run on main @ 925ea1d: bash scripts/integration-gate.sh returns GATE PASS with all 12 blocking checks at exit 0, including typecheck, build, the 140-test contract suite and the 28 approval-policy tests.

GROK's point 1 remains true and is a gap in this deliverable, not a procedural blocker: THREAT_MODEL.md line 370 declares the prompt-injection tests T-SEC-1 as not implemented, and the 28 green tests cover the approval policy only.

The approval policy is executable code rather than a table a model must interpret: evaluateApproval is a pure function and each of the ten override rules OV-1..OV-10 has a test that deliberately violates it. 28 tests pass.

TH-10 (proof fabrication) is rated CRITICA for severity and ALTA for probability and remains partially open: P0-1 prevents an agent from fabricating the attestation that a tool was called, but does not prevent an agent from inflating its own ResultEnvelope.

S-28, found and closed in this session: the monotonicity checks were fail-open. `rankOf` used `indexOf`, which returns -1 outside the domain, and `-1 <= n` holds for every n, so the functions that impose the limit ceiling admitted whatever they did not recognise. Measured before the fix: autonomyWithin("L5","L2") was true, defeating this blueprint's own claim that L5 is unreachable by a manifest. A manifest is JSON and JSON arrives as strings, so the type system did not survive the wire. The same indexOf-as-rank shape existed at five sites; four were fail-open and were corrected in one place, and the fifth (resolveCostClass) was already fail-closed and serves as the positive control. Regression tests in tests/threat-model/prompt-injection.test.mjs, wired into the integration gate as blocking.

decisions_proposed.proposal: Do not accept weight on UJ-SEC-001 in this session even though the independent reviewer passed both acceptance criteria and the author holds the acceptance mandate. The reviewer conditioned acceptance on commands that only the integrator can run, and in this program the integrator and the author are the same actor, so discharging that condition alone would collapse an independent check into a self-check.
